title: FairPrice Discounts: Save Up to 36% on House Brand Products in Singapore (March-June 2024)
text:
Singaporean shoppers are set to benefit from discounts on a wide range of everyday essentials as FairPrice launches a 12-week campaign offering reduced prices on its house-brand products. Starting March 19, 2026, and running through June 10, 2026, the initiative aims to assist families manage rising costs and stretch their budgets further, particularly on frequently purchased items like rice, facial tissue, and frozen processed foods. This move comes as many households continue to navigate economic uncertainty and increasing expenses.
The discounts, reaching up to 36 percent, will be applied to a rotating selection of FairPrice house-brand items each week. In the initial week, shoppers can expect savings on canola oil, bacon, kitchen towels, and facial tissue, among other products. FairPrice currently offers over 3,500 own-brand products, which are typically priced 10 to 15 percent lower than comparable branded alternatives, providing a significant cost-saving opportunity for consumers.
FairPrice Best Sellers for Less: A Response to Economic Pressures This campaign, known as FairPrice Best Sellers for Less, isn’t a new initiative. It was initially launched in 2025 as part of the celebrations surrounding Singapore’s 60th year of independence, SG60. However, FairPrice Group has brought it back due to the ongoing economic challenges faced by Singaporeans. The supermarket chain recognizes the need to provide affordable options for essential goods during a period of economic uncertainty.
Vipul Chawla, chief executive of FairPrice Group, emphasized the company’s commitment to its customers. He stated that FairPrice hopes to “repay Singaporeans for the trust they place in its own brands and to assure them that it is committed to keeping quality staples affordable during times of uncertainty.” This sentiment underscores FairPrice’s role as a key player in ensuring food security and affordability for the nation.
Who Benefits from the Discounts? The discounts are available to all shoppers at FairPrice supermarkets across Singapore. However, additional benefits are available to specific groups. Blue CHAS (Community Health Assist Scheme) cardholders will receive a 3% discount every Thursday, while CHAS Orange cardholders will enjoy the same benefit on Fridays. Pioneer and Merdeka Generation members are eligible for an additional 3% off on Mondays and Wednesdays, and Senior Citizens will receive an extra 2% off on Tuesdays. These ongoing discounts complement the FairPrice Best Sellers for Less campaign, offering multiple avenues for savings.
Understanding FairPrice House Brands FairPrice house brands have become increasingly popular among Singaporean consumers, offering a balance of quality and affordability. With over 3,500 products available, these brands cover a wide range of grocery categories, from pantry staples to household cleaning supplies. The price difference – typically 10 to 15 percent lower than branded alternatives – can add up to substantial savings over time, especially for families with larger grocery bills.
Looking Ahead: Weekly Updates and Continued Savings Shoppers are encouraged to check FairPrice stores and online platforms each week to discover the latest products included in the Best Sellers for Less campaign. The rotating selection ensures a variety of savings opportunities throughout the 12-week period. FairPrice has not yet announced specific details about the products that will be featured in subsequent weeks, but promises a continued focus on essential items.
The FairPrice Best Sellers for Less campaign is a timely response to the economic pressures facing Singaporean households. By offering discounts on its house-brand products, FairPrice aims to provide much-needed relief to shoppers and demonstrate its commitment to affordability and value. The next update on participating products will be available on March 26, 2026.
